headline: Requires Homeland Security to review large contracts for services along the U.S.-Mexico land border and report its findings to Congress.
what_it_does: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) must send Congress a report on active contracts worth $50 million or more for services along the U.S. land border with Mexico. The report must explain how DHS decides when it needs contractor workers, what those workers do and where, and what benefits they provide. It must also include a five-year strategy for improving these contracts, along with recommendations. DHS must submit a plan to carry out the recommendations and brief Congress on its progress.

who_it_affects.how: DHS must study its large border service contracts, write a report and plan, and update Congress on its progress.

who_it_affects.group: Companies with large DHS border service contracts
who_it_affects.how: Their contracts worth $50 million or more will be reviewed, and future contracts may change based on DHS's recommendations.
They will receive the report, the plan, and briefings on how DHS uses contractors at the southern border.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; the summary does not give a specific deadline for the report.
